§6.4 Marginal Notes

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-marginal-notes · layout rule structure legal

✅ Normative

Each printed marginal note MUST be rendered as a separate block placed immediately after the element it annotates. Where the element it belongs to cannot be established, the note MUST still be kept as a separate block and MUST NOT be merged into body text.

Statutes and some textbooks print short notes in the outer margin — a citation, a one-word gloss — aligned with the line they annotate. They are printed text, not handwriting, and they belong to a particular line.

SEC. 105. INVESTIGATIONS AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEEDINGS.        15 USC 7215.
   (a) IN GENERAL.—The Board shall establish, by rule, …      Establishment.

Requirements

  • A marginal note MUST be its own element, never part of the heading or paragraph it sits beside.
  • It MUST follow the element it annotates — the heading or paragraph level with it — in reading order, before the next element of the body.
  • A geometric reading that inserts 15 USC 7215. into the middle of the section heading, or splices a gloss into a line of the paragraph, does not conform.

✅ Sample — a public law with sidenotes


Source: Public Law 107-204 (Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002), 116 Stat. 759, §105 marginal notes (public domain)

15 USC 7215. and Establishment. in the right margin, level with SEC. 105. and (a) IN GENERAL.; the body is set in one narrower column. The small capitals of IN GENERAL are transcribed as capitals. The heading depth is relative: the page does not show the outline above the section.
